summary: This change deliberately loosens a security guard, so the lens applied is: what NEW capability does the allowlisted lane gain? Only this — a read-only companion task may read one repo-contained regular file as its prompt. Exfiltration via absolute/traversal/symlink-escape paths is refused with both sides resolved before comparison; dangling and directory targets are refused by is_file; duplicate flags and missing values cannot smuggle a second interpretation; the equals form cannot reach the admission because '=' is refused as shell syntax upstream (pinned by a test). Write-shaped invocations, wrappers, and shell metacharacters are refused exactly as before — the sandbox mode still derives from argv shape, never from prompt content.
residual_risks: Prompt content can still instruct the model arbitrarily — unchanged trust shape: read-only sandboxing, not content vetting, is what bounds a rescue run, exactly as with delegate-composed briefs.
